draft.title: What world order means
card: World order is the set of rules, institutions and relationships that help keep peace and security between countries.
Rules
agreed standards of behaviour for states, such as treaties and international law.
Institutions
organisations that states set up to work together, such as the United Nations.
Relationships
the alliances, trade links and diplomacy that connect countries and give them reasons to cooperate.
draft.remember: World order is rules, institutions and relationships working together to keep countries at peace.

a.q: Which statement best describes world order?
opts: Rules, institutions and relationships that keep states at peace
A single world government that makes laws for every country
The military power held by the largest country in the world
The laws that each country makes to govern its own people
a.why: World order is the combination of rules, institutions and relationships that help keep peace and security between countries. The option about one world government is tempting, but world order does not need a single government, as states work through shared rules and organisations.
a.clue: Think of what links countries, not what rules inside one country.

b.q: Two neighbouring countries sign a treaty on their border and agree to take any future dispute to an international organisation. Which part of world order does the agreement to use the organisation show?
opts: Institutions
Rules
Relationships
Domestic law
b.why: An international organisation is an institution that states set up to work together, so using one is an example of institutions. The treaty itself is a rule, which is the tempting option, but the question asks about the organisation.
b.clue: Which part is an organisation, not an agreed standard?
